items.summary:
ONE token turned a $0.40 AI request into $0.80.

and 4 "cheap" $20 subscriptions quietly cost $1,080 a year.

so i wrote 98 lines of python to audit what AI actually costs. real published prices, no vibes.

it said cut $360. the cache line alone was -88%.

here's what nobody checks.

ChatGPT Plus $20. Claude Pro $20. SuperGrok $30. Cursor Pro $20.
$90 a month. $1,080 a year. before tax.

each one looks reasonable the day you click subscribe. the bill only shows up when they stack

what the script printed, prices as of Aug 28, US web:

> 5M input + 1M output tokens a month: Sonnet 5 $20.00, Grok 4.6 $16.00, GPT-5.6 Luna $2.20
> use 1/5 of that and Sonnet is $4. not $20
> keep 2 subs + a $20 API budget: $720/yr. saves $360
> agent sending the same 100K prompt 50 times: $10.00 naive, $1.23 cached. -88%
> batch API: half price if you can wait
> Grok 4.6 at 199,999 tokens: $0.40. at 200,000: $0.80. one token doubles the whole request
> 20K records to JSON: $160 on Sol, $8.80 on Luna (my assumption: 1K in / 200 out each)

the lesson isn't "API is cheaper". heavy users burn $20 of API in days. the lesson is most people never did the math

how to audit yours:
1. list every AI sub and what you actually use it for
2. split the product (IDE, bots, connectors) from the model access
3. log 30 days of how often you open each one
4. move the occasional ones to pay-per-token
5. cache stable prompts, batch what can wait, watch the 200K / 272K cliffs
6. route easy work to cheap models, keep the frontier one for hard problems

every subscription has to earn its spot on your card. my math on published prices, not financial advice

items.title: Anthropic 发布 Claude 模型选型指南，建议开发者不要默认使用最强的 Fable 5.2。大多数编程和知识工作从 Opus 5.5 的 Medium 推理强度开始。需求明确的功能开发、日常自动化可以使用更便宜的 Sonnet
items.summary:
Anthropic 发布 Claude 模型选型指南，建议开发者不要默认使用最强的 Fable 5.2。大多数编程和知识工作从 Opus 5.5 的 Medium 推理强度开始。需求明确的功能开发、日常自动化可以使用更便宜的 Sonnet 5.5；分类、信息提取等简单任务交给 Haiku 5.5。大型代码迁移、复杂科研，或者 Opus 难以完成的任务，再考虑 Fable 5.2。

Anthropic 认为，降低成本的一个有效方法是让 AI 自己检查结果。例如编程时运行自动化测试，发现错误再修改，而不是一开始就使用最高推理强度。

官方在 SWE-bench Pro 编程测试的同一子集上，让 Opus 5.5 先用 Low 推理强度执行，只把失败的任务交给 High 重试。结果通过率达到约 97%，平均每题成本 0.17 美元；全部直接使用 High，通过率为 95.3%，每题成本 0.29 美元。前者成本降低约 41%，通过率还略高。

单纯增加推理强度的性价比也有上限。Opus 5.5 从 High 提升至 Xhigh，在 SWE-bench Pro 上的成绩只提高约 1.4 个百分点，成本却达到原来的 2.5 倍。Anthropic 建议，模型达到 High 后仍无法解决难题，可以尝试更强模型的较低推理强度。

例如在 FrontierCode 2.0 编程评测中，Fable 5.2 使用 High 获得 45.3%，几乎追平 Opus 5.5 使用 Max 时的 45.5%，平均每题成本却只有后者约一半。虽然 Fable 的 API Token 单价是 Opus 的两倍，但在这类高难度任务中，完成任务的总成本反而可能更低。

items.summary:
Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20 years of HN to 6,454 videos that keep being recommended. *Significantly* better viewing experience, ~2 hours with Opus 5.5:
https://t.co/JIhXN7OSh1

- Excellent recs without any logins (state is kept in local browser session)
- Thumbnail is a representative frame from middle of the video instead of the super duper A/B test hyper-optimized user uploads
- Underlying data from the comment analysis as one zip file, point your Claude at it and ask for your own version
- HackerTube Longs ✊

A bit more on the process:
I use Claude Code (desktop app for Mac), Opus 5.5 on Medium effort as my default. I only talk to Claude and have it do everything, the only "manual work" I helped with in tandem was in the browser (reminiscent of MenuGen): 1) I had to create some kind of API key from Google Cloud UI to query YouTube for video metadata, 2) I booted up a VPS box for serving and 3) I bought the domain name. Once the box was up I gave Claude the IP and told it update, secure, harden, deploy and optimize the code, and it did the whole thing.

Many awesome projects that would have normally taken weeks/months even can now be few-shotted for breakfast. What else are we not thinking of.

items.title: Setting a new standard for responsible AI infrastructure | OpenAI
items.summary: The promise of AI is that it gives people more power to shape their own futures. It can help someone learn a new skill, build a business, or solve a problem that was previously out of reach. Building more computing infrastructure capacity in the United States can help lower the cost of delivering AI, put these tools in more people’s hands, and ensure America stays at the forefront of the technology. [...] protect residents, and ensure that the benefits of AI infrastructure are broadly shared. [...] Create opportunities for local workers and businesses.We’ll publish the jobs we expect to create, work with unions and training providers to help residents prepare for them, and report annually on hiring and apprenticeships. We’ll also make sustained investments in priorities residents help select.

items.title: OpenAI to pay for data center power after election shows AI concern
items.summary: OpenAI reaffirmed its promise to pay the full cost of powering data centers as part of a series of commitments the company published Thursday, two days after voters at the polls roundly rejected the rapid expansion of AI. [...] AI companies like OpenAI depend on AI data centers to serve customers and develop new models, and they're seeking to build out as rapidly as possible to meet demand. In February, OpenAI told investors that it's targeting $600 billion in total compute spend by 2030, and the company has since announced massive data center projects in Georgia and Ohio. [...] OpenAI has repeatedly pledged to protect ratepayers and invest in local communities this year, and Lehane said the company's latest commitments build on many of its previous initiatives. He said the policy blueprint has been in the works since August, and that he met with dozens of lawmakers and candidates since then.

OpenAI and Anthropic have tried to ​maintain a more open research culture to both ⁠attract employees and foster creativity that can lead to breakthroughs. The AI field is rooted in academia, where machine-learning scientists have openly discussed their research.
